sanskrit: sannātmā naiva dharmasya na parasya na cātmanaḥ sarvopāyair ujjihīrṣed ātmānam iti niścayaḥ
english: The man whose self is composed should, by every means, strive to raise himself up—neither for the sake of dharma, nor for another, nor merely for his own self; this is the settled conclusion.

sanskrit: tatra dharmavidāṃ tāta niścayo dharmanaipuṇe udyamo jīvanaṃ kṣatre bāhuvīryād iti śrutiḥ
english: Herein, my son, lies the conviction of those skilled in dharma, in the subtleties of righteousness: that exertion is the livelihood of the warrior, and that he lives by the might of his arms—so runs the sacred teaching.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo vṛttisaṃrodhe kasya nādātum arhati anyatra tāpasasvāc ca brāhmaṇasvāc ca bhārata
english: When his means of livelihood are blocked, from whom may a kṣatriya not take what he needs—save only from the property of an ascetic and the property of a brāhmaṇa, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: yathā vai brāhmaṇaḥ sīdann ayājyam api yājayet abhojyānnāni cāśnīyāt tathedaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Just as a brāhmaṇa, sinking into distress, may officiate at sacrifices even for those unworthy of his ministry and may eat forbidden food, so too is it in this case—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: pīḍitasya kim advāram utpatho nidhṛtasya vā advārataḥ pradravati yadā bhavati pīḍitaḥ
english: For one hard-pressed, what door is barred, what path forbidden to one held down? When a man is sorely pressed, he breaks out even where there is no proper door.

sanskrit: tasya kośabalajyānyā sarvalokaparābhavaḥ bhaikṣacaryā na vihitā na ca viṭśūdrajīvikā
english: With the loss of his treasury and his army comes defeat before all the world; yet for him the life of a beggar is not ordained, nor the livelihood of a vaiśya or a śūdra.

sanskrit: svadharmānantarā vṛttir yānyān anupajīvataḥ vahataḥ prathamaṃ kalpam anukalpena jīvanam
english: For one who does not depend upon others, the livelihood nearest to his own dharma is right; pursuing first the primary rule, he may live by the secondary rule in its stead.

sanskrit: āpadgatena dharmāṇām anyāyenopajīvanam api hy etad brāhmaṇeṣu dṛṣṭaṃ vṛttiparikṣaye
english: For one fallen into calamity, even a livelihood gained by irregular means among the rules of dharma is allowed; indeed this has been seen even among brāhmaṇas when their means of living are exhausted.

sanskrit: kṣatriye saṃśayaḥ kaḥ syād ity etan niścitaṃ sadā ādadīta viśiṣṭebhyo nāvasīdet kathaṃ cana
english: What doubt, then, could there be in the case of a kṣatriya? This is ever certain: let him take from those who have more, and let him in no way sink into ruin.

sanskrit: hantāraṃ rakṣitāraṃ ca prajānāṃ kṣatriyaṃ viduḥ tasmāt saṃrakṣatā kāryam ādānaṃ kṣatrabandhunā
english: The kṣatriya is known as both the slayer and the protector of the people; therefore, while guarding them, the kinsman of the warrior-order must take what is needful.

sanskrit: anyatra rājan hiṃsāyā vṛttir nehāsti kasya cit apy araṇyasamutthasya ekasya carato muneḥ
english: Apart from doing harm, O king, there is no livelihood here for anyone—not even for the lone sage who roams and subsists upon what springs up in the forest.

sanskrit: na śaṅkhalikhitāṃ vṛttiṃ śakyam āsthāya jīvitum viśeṣataḥ kuruśreṣṭha prajāpālanam īpsatā
english: One cannot live by adopting the way of life laid down by Śaṅkha and Likhita—least of all, O best of the Kurus, by one who desires to protect the people.

sanskrit: parasparābhisaṃrakṣā rājñā rāṣṭreṇa cāpadi nityam eveha kartavyā eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: In time of calamity, mutual protection must always be practiced here between the king and the kingdom: this is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: rājā rāṣṭraṃ yathāpatsu dravyaughaiḥ parirakṣati rāṣṭreṇa rājā vyasane parirakṣyas tathā bhavet
english: As the king in times of distress guards the kingdom with his abundant wealth, so too, when calamity strikes, must the king be protected by the kingdom.

sanskrit: kośaṃ daṇḍaṃ balaṃ mitraṃ yad anyad api saṃcitam na kurvītāntaraṃ rāṣṭre rājā parigate kṣudhā
english: When his kingdom is overtaken by famine, the king should not hold back his treasury, his army of punishment, his forces, his allies, or whatever else he has stored up.

sanskrit: bījaṃ bhaktena saṃpādyam iti dharmavido viduḥ atraitac chambarasyāhur mahāmāyasya darśanam
english: Those who know dharma understand that the seed-grain must be procured through devoted service; and here they cite the teaching of Śambara, the master of great illusions.

sanskrit: dhik tasya jīvitaṃ rājño rāṣṭre yasyāvasīdati avṛttyāntyamanuṣyo 'pi yo vai veda śiber vacaḥ
english: Shame upon the life of that king in whose realm even the lowest of men perishes for lack of livelihood—he who has truly heeded the words of Śibi.

sanskrit: rājñaḥ kośabalaṃ mūlaṃ kośamūlaṃ punar balam tan mūlaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmamūlāḥ punaḥ prajāḥ
english: The king's foundation is the strength of his treasury; and the treasury, in turn, is the root of his army; that army is the root of all observances of dharma; and the people, in turn, are the root of dharma itself.

sanskrit: nānyān apīḍayitveha kośaḥ śakyaḥ kuto balam tadarthaṃ pīḍayitvā ca doṣaṃ na prāptum arhati
english: Without pressing upon others here, no treasury can be amassed—and whence then an army? Yet one who presses upon them for this purpose ought to incur no fault.

sanskrit: akāryam api yajñārthaṃ kriyate yajñakarmasu etasmāt kāraṇād rājā na doṣaṃ prāptum arhati
english: Even what ought not to be done is done for the sake of sacrifice in the rites of sacrifice; for this same reason the king ought to incur no fault.

sanskrit: arthārtham anyad bhavati viparītam athāparam anarthārtham athāpy anyat tat sarvaṃ hy arthalakṣaṇam evaṃ buddhyā saṃprapaśyen medhāvī kāryaniścayam
english: One thing serves a worthy end; another, contrary to it, serves no worthy end; yet another serves a positively harmful end—all of these, indeed, bear the mark of purpose. Thus with his intellect should the wise man clearly discern what action to resolve upon.

sanskrit: yajñārtham anyad bhavati yajñe nārthas tathāparaḥ yajñasyārthārtham evānyat tat sarvaṃ yajñasādhanam
english: One thing serves the purpose of sacrifice; in another there is no purpose for the sacrifice; yet another serves the very means of the sacrifice—all of these are instruments of sacrifice.

sanskrit: upamām atra vakṣyāmi dharmatattvaprakāśinīm yūpaṃ chindanti yajñārthaṃ tatra ye paripanthinaḥ
english: Here I shall set forth a comparison that illumines the truth of dharma: men fell a tree to make the sacrificial post; and those trees that stand in the way—

sanskrit: drumāḥ ke cana sāmantā dhruvaṃ chindanti tān api te cāpi nipatanto 'nyān nighnanti ca vanaspatīn
english: —certain trees standing close beside it they surely cut down as well; and these, in falling, strike down still other forest trees.

sanskrit: evaṃ kośasya mahato ye narāḥ paripanthinaḥ tān ahatvā na paśyāmi siddhim atra paraṃtapa
english: Just so, O scorcher of foes, those men who stand in the way of a great treasury—without striking them down I see no success to be had in this matter.

sanskrit: dhanena jayate lokāv ubhau param imaṃ tathā satyaṃ ca dharmavacanaṃ yathā nāsty adhanas tathā
english: By wealth one wins both worlds, the world beyond and this one here; and it is a true word of dharma that the man without wealth is as though he were not at all.

sanskrit: sarvopāyair ādadīta dhanaṃ yajñaprayojanam na tulyadoṣaḥ syād evaṃ kāryākāryeṣu bhārata
english: By every means let him take wealth for the purpose of sacrifice; the fault is not the same, O Bhārata, in things to be done and things not to be done.

sanskrit: naitau saṃbhavato rājan kathaṃ cid api bhārata na hy araṇyeṣu paśyāmi dhanavṛddhān ahaṃ kva cit
english: These two, O king, can in no way coexist, O Bhārata; for nowhere in the forests do I ever see men grown rich.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ dṛśyate vittaṃ pṛthivyām iha kiṃ cana mamedaṃ syān mamedaṃ syād ity ayaṃ kāṅkṣate janaḥ
english: Whatever wealth is seen here upon the earth, this man hankers after it, thinking, 'This should be mine, this should be mine.'

sanskrit: na ca rājyasamo dharmaḥ kaś cid asti paraṃtapa dharmaṃ śaṃsanti te rājñām āpadartham ito 'nyathā
english: There is no dharma equal to kingship, O scorcher of foes; the wise commend kingship as the dharma of kings—save where calamity dictates otherwise than this.

sanskrit: dānena karmaṇā cānye tapasānye tapasvinaḥ buddhyā dākṣyeṇa cāpy anye cinvanti dhanasaṃcayān
english: Some amass their hoards of wealth by giving and by ritual works, the ascetics by austerity, and yet others by intellect and skill.

sanskrit: adhanaṃ durbalaṃ prāhur dhanena balavān bhavet sarvaṃ dhanavataḥ prāpyaṃ sarvaṃ tarati kośavān kośād dharmaś ca kāmaś ca paro lokas tathāpy ayam
english: They call the man without wealth weak; through wealth a man grows strong. All things are attainable by the wealthy; the man with a treasury crosses every difficulty. From the treasury flow dharma and desire, the world beyond and this world too.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kṣīṇasya dīrghasūtrasya sānukrośasya bandhuṣu viraktapaurarāṣṭrasya nirdravyanicayasya ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For a king grown weak, slow to act, tender-hearted toward his kinsmen, whose townsfolk and countryfolk have turned against him, and whose stores of wealth are gone—

sanskrit: pariśaṅkitamukhyasya srutamantrasya bhārata asaṃbhāvitamitrasya bhinnāmātyasya sarvaśaḥ
english: —whose chief ministers are suspect, O Bhārata, whose counsel has leaked out, who can win no allies, and whose counselors are wholly divided—

sanskrit: paracakrābhiyātasya durbalasya balīyasā āpannacetaso brūhi kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣyate
english: —assailed by an enemy host, weak before a stronger foe, his mind sunk in calamity: tell me, what course of action yet remains?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca bāhyaś ced vijigīṣuḥ syād dharmārthakuśalaḥ śuciḥ javena saṃdhiṃ kurvīta pūrvān pūrvān vimokṣayan
english: Bhīṣma said: If the would-be conqueror be an outside foe, skilled in dharma and statecraft and pure of conduct, let the king swiftly make peace with him, releasing his prisoners one after another.

sanskrit: adharmavijigīṣuś ced balavān pāpaniścayaḥ ātmanaḥ saṃnirodhena saṃdhiṃ tenābhiyojayet
english: But if the would-be conqueror be a man of unrighteous aims, strong and set upon wickedness, then by restraining himself the king should bind that one to a treaty.

sanskrit: apāsya rājadhānīṃ vā tared anyena vāpadam tadbhāvabhāve dravyāṇi jīvan punar upārjayet
english: Or else, abandoning his capital, he may cross over the calamity by some other means; for whether it endures or passes, he, while yet alive, may earn his wealth anew.

sanskrit: yās tu syuḥ kevalatyāgāc chakyās taritum āpadaḥ kas tatrādhikam ātmānaṃ saṃtyajed arthadharmavit
english: As for those calamities that can be crossed by mere renunciation of possessions—what man who knows wealth and dharma would there cast away his own self, which is worth more?

sanskrit: avarodhāj jugupseta kā sapatnadhane dayā na tv evātmā pradātavyaḥ śakye sati kathaṃ cana
english: Let him shrink from being made captive; what pity is there for a rival's wealth? Yet so long as it can be avoided, the self must in no way be surrendered.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ābhyantare prakupite bāhye copanipīḍite kṣīṇe kośe srute mantre kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When the inner realm is in revolt and the outer is hard-pressed, when the treasury is drained and the counsel has leaked away—what course of action yet remains?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kṣipraṃ vā saṃdhikāmaḥ syāt kṣipraṃ vā tīkṣṇavikramaḥ padāpanayanaṃ kṣipram etāvat sāṃparāyikam
english: Bhīṣma said: Let him swiftly seek peace, or else be swiftly fierce in valor; or let him swiftly withdraw his footing—this much is the wisdom for the hour of crisis.

sanskrit: anuraktena puṣṭena hṛṣṭena jagatīpate alpenāpi hi sainyena mahīṃ jayati pārthivaḥ
english: With an army that is devoted, well-nourished, and high in spirit, O lord of the earth, a king conquers the world even with but a small force.

sanskrit: hato vā divam ārohed vijayī kṣitim āvaset yuddhe tu saṃtyajan prāṇāñ śakrasyaiti salokatām
english: Slain, he ascends to heaven; victorious, he dwells upon the earth; but he who lays down his life in battle attains to the same world as Indra.

sanskrit: sarvalokāgamaṃ kṛtvā mṛdutvaṃ gantum eva ca viśvāsād vinayaṃ kuryād vyavasyed vāpy upānahau
english: Having gauged the temper of all the people and chosen the path of gentleness, the king should, to win their trust, conduct himself with humility, or else resolve to put on his marching sandals.

sanskrit: apakramitum icched vā yathākāmaṃ tu sāntvayet viliṅgamitvā mitreṇa tataḥ svayam upakramet
english: Or, should he wish to withdraw, let him conciliate as he pleases; and having gone in disguise with an ally, let him then himself set out to act.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca hīne paramake dharme sarvalokātilaṅghini sarvasmin dasyusād bhūte pṛthivyām upajīvane
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When the highest dharma has decayed and lawlessness oversteps all the world, when every means of livelihood upon the earth has fallen prey to robbers—

sanskrit: kenāsmin brāhmaṇo jīvej jaghanye kāla āgate asaṃtyajan putrapautrān anukrośāt pitāmaha
english: —by what means, O grandfather, is a brāhmaṇa to live in such a time, when the basest of ages has come, without abandoning, out of tenderness, his sons and grandsons?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vijñānabalam āsthāya jīvitavyaṃ tathāgate sarvaṃ sādhvartham evedam asādhvarthaṃ na kiṃ cana
english: Bhīṣma said: When such a time has come, one must live by relying upon the power of discernment. All of this is for a good end; nothing of it is for an ill end.

sanskrit: asādhubhyo nirādāya sādhubhyo yaḥ prayacchati ātmānaṃ saṃkramaṃ kṛtvā kṛtsnadharmavid eva saḥ
english: He who takes from the wicked and bestows upon the good, making of himself a bridge between them—he indeed is one who knows dharma entire.

sanskrit: suroṣeṇātmano rājan rājye sthitim akopayan adattam apy ādadīta dātur vittaṃ mameti vā
english: With righteous indignation, O king, not disturbing the stability of his own rule, he may take even what was not given, holding the giver's wealth to be his own.

sanskrit: vijñānabalapūto yo vartate ninditeṣv api vṛttavijñānavān dhīraḥ kas taṃ kiṃ vaktum arhati
english: Of one who, purified by the power of discernment, moves even among censured deeds—steadfast, accomplished in conduct and discernment—who is fit to say anything against him?

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ balakṛtā vṛttir naiṣām anyābhirocate tejasābhipravardhante balavanto yudhiṣṭhira
english: Those whose livelihood is wrought by strength take pleasure in no other; they grow ever greater through their splendor, the mighty ones, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yad eva prakṛtaṃ śāstram aviśeṣeṇa vindati tad eva madhyāḥ sevante medhāvī cāpy athottaram
english: Whatever ordinary teaching is grasped without discrimination, that the middling sort follow; but the wise man pursues, beyond it, the higher truth.

sanskrit: ṛtvikpurohitācāryān satkṛtair abhipūjitān na brāhmaṇān yātayeta doṣān prāpnoti yātayan
english: His officiating priests, his household priest, his teachers—the honored brāhmaṇas worshiped with due rites—the king should not harass; harassing them, he incurs grievous faults.

sanskrit: etat pramāṇaṃ lokasya cakṣur etat sanātanam tat pramāṇo 'vagāheta tena tat sādhv asādhu vā
english: These are the standard for the world, these the eternal eye; taking them for his measure, let the king plumb the matter, and by them judge it good or ill.

sanskrit: bahūni grāmavāstavyā roṣād brūyuḥ parasparam na teṣāṃ vacanād rājā satkuryād yātayeta vā
english: Many are the things that village-dwellers say against one another in anger; on the strength of their words the king should neither honor a man nor punish him.

sanskrit: na vācyaḥ parivādo vai na śrotavyaḥ kathaṃ cana karṇāv eva pidhātavyau prastheyaṃ vā tato 'nyataḥ
english: Slander should never be spoken, nor in any way listened to; rather, one should stop one's ears, or go away to some other place.

sanskrit: na vai satāṃ vṛttam etat parivādo na paiśunam guṇānām eva vaktāraḥ santaḥ satsu yudhiṣṭhira
english: This is not the conduct of the good—neither slander nor talebearing; the good, O Yudhiṣṭhira, speak only of the virtues that are in the good.

sanskrit: yathā samadhurau damyau sudāntau sādhuvāhinau dhuram udyamya vahatas tathā varteta vai nṛpaḥ yathā yathāsya vahataḥ sahāyāḥ syus tathāpare
english: As two trained oxen, evenly yoked, well-broken and drawing true, take up the yoke and bear it, so should the king conduct himself; and as his helpers bear their share, so let the others bear theirs likewise.

sanskrit: ācāram eva manyante garīyo dharmalakṣaṇam apare naivam icchanti ye śaṅkhalikhitapriyāḥ mārdavād atha lobhād vā te brūyur vākyam īdṛśam
english: Some hold right conduct to be the weightier mark of dharma; others, who delight in the way of Śaṅkha and Likhita, do not think so. Whether out of softness or out of greed, those latter would speak words of this kind.

sanskrit: ārṣam apy atra paśyanti vikarmasthasya yāpanam na cārṣāt sadṛśaṃ kiṃ cit pramāṇaṃ vidyate kva cit
english: In this they see even sage-given authority for sustaining the man who strays into forbidden deeds; and nowhere is any standard found equal to that of the sages.

sanskrit: devā api vikarmasthaṃ yātayanti narādhamam vyājena vindan vittaṃ hi dharmāt tu parihīyate
english: Even the gods chastise the basest of men who persists in forbidden deeds; for one who gains wealth by deceit falls away from dharma.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ satkṛtaḥ sadbhir bhūtiprabhavakāraṇaiḥ hṛdayenābhyanujñāto yo dharmas taṃ vyavasyati
english: That dharma which is honored on every side by the good, who are the source and cause of prosperity, and which is sanctioned by one's own heart—upon that let a man resolve.

sanskrit: yaś caturguṇasaṃpannaṃ dharmaṃ veda sa dharmavit aher iva hi dharmasya padaṃ duḥkhaṃ gaveṣitum
english: He who knows dharma endowed with its fourfold quality is the true knower of dharma; for the track of dharma, like that of a snake, is hard to trace out.

sanskrit: yathā mṛgasya viddhasya mṛgavyādhaḥ padaṃ nayet kakṣe rudhirapātena tathā dharmapadaṃ nayet
english: As the hunter follows the trail of a wounded deer through the thicket by the falling of its blood, so should one follow out the track of dharma.

sanskrit: evaṃ sadbhir vinītena pathā gantavyam acyuta rājarṣīṇāṃ vṛttam etad avagaccha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Thus, O unfaltering one, must one walk by the path made smooth by the good; understand this to be the conduct of royal sages, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca svarāṣṭrāt pararāṣṭrāc ca kośaṃ saṃjanayen nṛpaḥ kośād dhi dharmaḥ kaunteya rājyamūlaḥ pravartate
english: Bhīṣma said: From his own realm and from the realm of his foe the king should raise his treasury; for from the treasury, O son of Kuntī, dharma, whose root is kingship, proceeds.

sanskrit: tasmāt saṃjanayet kośaṃ saṃhṛtya paripālayet paripālyānugṛhṇīyād eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Therefore let him raise a treasury, and having gathered it, let him guard it; and having guarded it, let him be gracious with it: this is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: na kośaḥ śuddhaśaucena na nṛśaṃsena jāyate padaṃ madhyamam āsthāya kośasaṃgrahaṇaṃ caret
english: A treasury arises neither through utter purity nor through cruelty; taking his stand upon the middle ground, the king should pursue the gathering of his treasury.

sanskrit: abalasya kutaḥ kośo hy akośasya kuto balam abalasya kuto rājyam arājñaḥ śrīḥ kuto bhavet
english: Whence a treasury for the weak? And whence strength for him who has no treasury? Whence a kingdom for the weak? And whence prosperity for one who is no king?

sanskrit: uccair vṛtteḥ śriyo hānir yathaiva maraṇaṃ tathā tasmāt kośaṃ balaṃ mitrāṇy atha rājā vivardhayet
english: For one of high station the loss of fortune is as death itself; therefore let the king ever increase his treasury, his forces, and his allies.

sanskrit: hīnakośaṃ hi rājānam avajānanti mānavāḥ na cāsyālpena tuṣyanti kāryam abhyutsahanti ca
english: Men despise a king whose treasury is depleted; they are not content with little from him, yet they grow bold to press their demands.

sanskrit: śriyo hi kāraṇād rājā satkriyāṃ labhate parām sāsya gūhati pāpāni vāso guhyam iva striyāḥ
english: It is by reason of his fortune that a king receives the highest honor; and that fortune conceals his faults, as a garment conceals the secret parts of a woman.

sanskrit: ṛddhim asyānuvartante purā viprakṛtā janāḥ śālāvṛkā ivājasraṃ jighāṃsūn iva vindati īdṛśasya kuto rājñaḥ sukhaṃ bharatasattama
english: The very people he once wronged now court his prosperity, yet he finds them ever like jackals, as though bent on his destruction. Whence, O best of the Bhāratas, can there be happiness for such a king?

sanskrit: udyacched eva na glāyed udyamo hy eva pauruṣam apy aparvaṇi bhajyeta na nameteha kasya cit
english: Let him strive on and never grow weary, for exertion itself is manliness; he would sooner break, even where there is no joint to break, than bend before anyone here.

sanskrit: apy araṇyaṃ samāśritya cared dasyugaṇaiḥ saha na tv evoddhṛtamaryādair dasyubhiḥ sahitaś caret dasyūnāṃ sulabhā senā raudrakarmasu bhārata
english: He may even take refuge in the forest and roam with bands of brigands, yet he should not consort with brigands who have cast off all restraint; for an army of brigands, O Bhārata, is easily had for deeds of terror.

sanskrit: ekāntena hy amaryādāt sarvo 'py udvijate janaḥ dasyavo 'py upaśaṅkante niranukrośakāriṇaḥ
english: From one who is utterly without restraint all people recoil; even brigands grow wary of those who act without any mercy.

sanskrit: sthāpayed eva maryādāṃ janacittaprasādinīm alpāpy atheha maryādā loke bhavati pūjitā
english: Let him therefore establish a restraint that gladdens the hearts of the people; for even a little restraint is honored here in the world.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ loko 'sti na para iti vyavasito janaḥ nālaṃ gantuṃ ca viśvāsaṃ nāstike bhayaśaṅkini
english: The man who has concluded, 'There is neither this world nor the next,' is not one in whom trust can ever be placed; for in a nihilist, fearful and suspicious, no confidence can rest.
